anchors.name: SIMPLE
anchors.text: Masha has 3 red balls and 2 blue balls. How many balls does she have?

anchors.name: HARDER_WORDS
anchors.text: A caterpillar crawls along a wooden fence. Every morning it climbs three metres, and every evening it slides down one metre. When does it reach the top?

anchors.name: LONG_SENTENCE
anchors.text: Tom and his little sister Ann walk to the big park by the river and see a lot of ducks and geese there. How many birds do they see?

anchors.name: VERY_LONG_SENTENCE
anchors.text: Tom and his little sister Ann walk to the big park by the river and they see a lot of ducks and a lot of geese there. How many birds do they see?

anchors.name: HARD
anchors.text: Every afternoon seven classmates exchange colourful postcards. Each classmate sends exactly one postcard to every other classmate. How many postcards are delivered altogether?

anchors.name: SPACESHIPS
anchors.text: Four spaceships dock in pairs. How many different pairs can they make?

anchors.name: SPACESHIPS_AGAIN
anchors.text: Four spaceships dock in pairs. How many different pairs can the ships make?

anchors.name: CLOCK
anchors.text: A clock strikes 3 times at three o'clock. How long does it strike at six o'clock?

source.note: Flesch-Kincaid applies to English only (the prototype's D42); the sentence limit to every language. The measurements here do not depend on the student's grade.
